lines.text: Maiden Lane began as a laundry path.
Its name means the maidens' path, from Dutch.
It began as a footpath beside a brook where women washed laundry.
The English kept the name after they took the town in 1664.

post.caption: Maiden Lane began as a laundry path. Its name means the maidens' path, from Dutch. It began as a footpath beside a brook where women washed laundry. The English kept the name after they took the town in 1664. By the late 1790s, jewelers had settled on the street. In 1894, developers finished the ten-story Diamond Exchange there. Its floors were strong enough to carry the dealers' safes. Big windows let dealers study stones in daylight. A jeweler's clock is set into the sidewalk at its corner. From the 1920s, the trade moved north to West 47th Street. That street is today's Diamond District.
